sentences.text: Scientists estimate this medium-sized sauropod weighed approximately 9,353 kilograms.
The animal measured twelve meters long and stood four meters tall, reaching a total mass of three tons.
It possessed a distinctive racquet-shaped scapula, a bone feature also found in other rebbachisaurids.
The genus was named by the Argentinian paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1996.
Bonaparte originally believed the fossil came from the Rayoso Formation, so he honored that location in the name.
The species name agrioensis refers to the Agrio River near the discovery site.
Later research in 2008 and 2009 determined the specimen actually came from the Candeleros Formation.
In 1998, Jeffrey Wilson and Paul Sereno proposed that the species Rebbachisaurus tessonei should be assigned to this genus.
There is an ongoing debate regarding whether Rayososaurus is a distinct genus given its extreme similarity to Rebbachisaurus.
Rayososaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately 99 to 95 million years ago in the Cenomanian stage.
The time range for this animal is the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago.
Calvo and Salgado consider Rayososaurus to be a nomen dubium, or a doubtful name.
Bonaparte defends the validity of Rayososaurus as the most basal member of the family Rebbachisauridae, citing the typical racquet-shaped scapula.
